suggestions.assertion: The report to the user is organized by symptom, not by word count
suggestions.reason: This passes for a baseline report organized by severity (Blocking / Missing / Padding / Minor). If 'by symptom' means the skill's specific symptom taxonomy, the assertion should say so; as written it is only discriminating against word-count-ordered output, which neither run produced.

The baseline's review is substantively strong (catches at-least-once/event_id semantics, concurrency cap vs the 2k rps incident, export scope, CSV format) and arguably more thorough than the with_skill rewrite, yet scores 3/6 solely because it did not write the file. That is the intended discrimination, but consider an explicit assertion 'the file was edited in place' so the three file-content failures are not conflated with a single root cause.

Three of six assertions fail for the same reason (no edit). Pass rate therefore measures 'did it edit' more than 'did it edit well'; a run that edits badly but keeps the scaffold out could score the same 6/6 as a good one.

eval_feedback.overall: Baseline flags both stale claims correctly and organizes by defect type, but never edits the file, so every edited-file assertion fails. Discrimination from with_skill comes entirely from the edit-vs-review split.
